chunks: 1744 - Al-Wassafi narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
"Among that with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, confidentially addressed Musa عليه السلام was that He said:"

"O Musa, honor the one who asks by giving a small amount or by a gracious reply. Indeed, there comes to you one who is neither human nor jinn, angels from among the angels of the Most Merciful, testing you concerning what I have entrusted to you, and asking you from what I have bestowed upon you. So consider how you will act, O son of 'Imran."

key_terms.الرَّحْمَنِ: the Most Merciful, a divine name emphasizing Allah's mercy
key_terms.السَّائِلَ: the one who asks, meaning a beggar or requester seeking help
key_terms.بَذْلٍ يَسِيرٍ: a small act of giving, indicating that even a little charity has value
key_terms.بِرَدٍّ جَمِيلٍ: a beautiful or gracious response, meaning a kind refusal without harshness
key_terms.خَوَّلْتُكَ: what I entrusted to you, referring to wealth or provision as a trust from Allah
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةٌ: angels, described here as testing human conduct
key_terms.نَوَّلْتُكَ: what I have granted you, meaning the blessings and provisions bestowed by Allah

ai.seo_question: How should one treat a beggar according to this hadith from Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a person who asks for help should be treated with dignity, whether through even a small gift or a kind refusal. It frames wealth as a trust from Allah عزّ وجلّ and presents encounters with the needy as moral tests, sometimes through angels who examine how one responds to what one has been given.
